Messages.Author: Oortje4ever
Messages.Body:
me and my opponent had a situation in which we could both see each
others hand.
i got a drawing out the beast but i like to use it for an other
combat.
my opponent has consealed-magnum in hand but doesnt want to play it
when i play dotb.
does the acting metuselah have to play it all first or can he wait and
play at any time before maneuvres are anounced?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


1.6.1.6 addresses this.

A. Acting Methuselah plays or passes.
B. If she plays, then go to A. If Pass, continue...
C. Blocking Methuselah plays of passes.
D. If she plays, then go to A. If Pass continue...
E. Begin maneuvering.

Messages.Author: reyda
Messages.Body:


LSJ 's response being quite technical, here is a simple one ;)

If you control the acting vampire, don't play the drawing out the beast.
Your opponent has the option to play the concealed magnum. If he plays it,
then you have the option to play drawing out the beast after this anyway.
(see rulebook and LSJ answer)

If you control the blocking vampire, you must wait to see if your opponent
plays the concealed magnum. If he doesn't do so , fine, you can decline to
play your drawing out the beast, he won't have the option to play it since
he didn't do it in the first place. (see rulebook and LSJ answer)

Messages.Author: reyda
Messages.Body:
Al wrote:

:: Hrm...correct me if I'm wrong, but if the acting minion's player

:: doesn't explicitly decline to play cards during prerange, he can
:: still play that drawing out the beast, right?

You are the defending player. You ask the acting player if he wants to play
something before range.

case 1: he says yes, plays his batch of prerange cards. Then he says 'up to
you'. Where you play your cards one by one, and the acting player can
interrupt your batch by playing other prerange cards he may have left. If
you had no cards to play before range, the acting player can't play the
cards he wanted since he said 'up to you'.

case 2 : he says no, then 'up to you'. You play your cards one by one, and
the acting player can interrupt your batch by playing other prerange cards
he may have left aside. If you play no prerange cards, then the acting
player can't go back on his decision to play zero cards.

do you get it ? =)
